title: ReMP: Low-Downtime Runtime Model-Parallelism Reconfiguration for LLM Serving
event_hint: ReMP: runtime model-parallelism reconfiguration framework for LLM serving
problem: Current LLM inference systems treat model parallelism topology (TP/PP) as static configuration, which conflicts with dynamically changing inference workloads. State-of-the-art systems lack online reconfiguration capabilities and can only switch configurations by restarting the service, resulting in several minutes of service interruption, KV cache loss, and prohibitive recomputation overhead.
mechanism: ReMP achieves dynamic TP/PP adjustment through three key techniques: (1) decoupling model parallelism topology from runtime state to avoid full service reconstruction; (2) two-dimensional KV cache migration mechanism to preserve reusable cache states after TP/PP changes; (3) end-to-end online reconfiguration using shared-memory model reloading, prebuilt parallel-state snapshots, and worker reuse. The MPU State Space preconstructs parallel-state snapshots for candidate topologies, moving process-group construction off the switching critical path. Worker lifecycle management classifies workers into active and standby states, avoiding CUDA runtime and model object reinitialization overhead.

evidence.claim: ReMP topology switching time on H100 platform
evidence.baseline: restart-based approach (several minutes of service interruption)
evidence.condition: Llama2-7B (~2s), Qwen3-30B-A3B (~5s), DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B (~5s), Llama2-70B (~8s), 8× H100 GPUs

evidence.claim: ReMP topology switching time on RTX 5090 platform
ReMP achieves 13-32% switching time reduction through KV transfer and model loading overlap
ReMP achieves lower TTFT and TPOT than fixed TP1PP8 and TP2PP4 configurations
evidence.condition: Under medium-to-high request pressure using BurstGPT-derived traces, all four models tested

evidence.claim: ReMP achieves higher output throughput than fixed TP1PP8 and TP2PP4 configurations
evidence.condition: Under medium-to-high request pressure using BurstGPT-derived traces, all four models tested

evaluation_context: Experiments conducted on two 8-GPU platforms (H100 and RTX 5090) using four representative LLMs from 7B to 70B parameters. Workload uses BurstGPT-derived request traces replayed under different request pressures. Comparisons made against restart-based reconfiguration baseline (qualitatively several minutes) and two fixed TP/PP configurations (TP1PP8 pipeline-heavy, TP2PP4 balanced). ReMP uses weighted selection metric combining output throughput, mean TPOT, and mean TTFT. Software implemented on vLLM V1.
limitations: Llama2-70B not evaluated on RTX 5090 due to GPU memory limitations. Evidence pack focuses on single-node or cluster-level reconfiguration without WAN/cross-region deployment validation. Restart baseline defined qualitatively as 'several minutes' without explicit time measurements in primary evidence. No production deployment validation or multi-tenant isolation analysis. KV cache migration overhead visible but WAN RTT/bandwidth constraints not evaluated. Two-dimensional KV cache migration mechanism (Figure 4) shows layer-wise streaming transfer with P2P KV slice transfer, but specific transfer data volumes not quantified. Fixed baselines (TP1PP8, TP2PP4) are representative deployment choices but may not cover all optimal configurations.
project_relevance: ReMP demonstrates KV cache migration across model parallelism topologies within a single cluster, with specific switching times now quantified: 1-8 seconds on H100 (1-4 seconds on RTX 5090) versus several minutes for restart-based approach. The two-dimensional KV cache migration mechanism provides insights for remote KV cache access patterns—PP changes move layers across pipeline stages, TP changes split or merge KV-head ranges, with layer-wise streaming transfer bounding peak GPU memory. However, the paper focuses on TP/PP reconfiguration for adaptive serving rather than cross-region transmission. WAN costs, compression, incremental transfer, and cross-region consistency are not addressed. Cache state preservation techniques and overlapping model reloading with KV migration (13-32% time savings) could inform cross-region cache migration strategies, though this application is beyond the paper's scope.
